data.body: Measured 2026-10-17 (load ~40, pytest -n 48): tests/test_uc_surf_loop_transcript.py::test_the_loop_cli_transcript_is_unchanged 126-130 s; the rest of the default [ci].always_tests set (DX-ci-always-run-guards) is ~30 s. The test has broken main so it stays in the set, but it alone makes every item's ci run ~2 min dearer. Make it cheaper (fewer subprocesses, in-process CLI) without loosening the pin. Also measured and kept OUT of the default: test_architecture_guards 18 s, test_compat* ~6 s each file, test_uc_surf_registry_rule_transcript 37 s.
data.title: uc_surf loop transcript test takes 130 s under load: make it cheap, it is in the ci always-run set

data.claim: An import closure never reaches the constants ratchet, transcripts or README tables; running a configured set apart from the selection catches them for about 30 s plus the loop transcript
data.falsifier: the default set run on a tree with a new knob fails nowhere, or costs under 90 s total
data.mechanism: those tests read the whole tree (constants audit, CLI output, config tables)
data.probe: pytest -n 48 on the 16 default files, before regenerating pins
data.probe_output: before pins regenerated: 4 failed (golden config --explain, readme_knob_table x2, setup_ops_transcript), 1281 passed; trimmed default set: 904 passed in 139 s (loop transcript 130 s of it, ex-loop ~30 s)
data.question: Does a selected ci run miss repo-wide guards, and what does an always set cost?

evidence.note: research CONFIRMED: new knob made 4 guard tests fail that a closure selector does not reach; default set 139 s under load 40, loop transcript 130 s
no [rules] violated: knob declared with doc, upgrade fragment added, no MCP tool, pins regenerated
ci_scope.always_tests, ci._execute second pytest run timed as always_s, [ci].always_tests knob + fragment, testscope covers always tests; tests/test_ci_always_tests.py

chunk_findings.detail: The doc text lists `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py` under "Not in the default, add them when they bite", but the same knob's default factory already contains `tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py` and `tests/test_uc_surf_loop_transcript.py`, both of which are matched by that pattern. So the documentation contradictorily presents an already-defaulted pattern as a not-in-default candidate: a user running `ddflow config --explain ci.always_tests` (or reading the knob list) is told to add a glob that is already covered by two explicit default entries, which misstates what "the default" contains and makes the guidance in that sentence unreliable for the other entries in the same list (`tests/test_architecture_guards.py`, `tests/test_compat*.py`). The concrete input demonstrating it is the default value itself: `tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py` ∈ factory default AND matches the pattern advertised as "not in the default".
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/ci.py:52 (the `always_tests` knob `doc`)

chunk_findings.detail: The loop reassigns `p` on every iteration, so `p.elapsed_s` on iteration *i* is only the elapsed time of iteration *i-1* — the elapsed time of the pre-hook result that was passed into the function (and of any command before the immediately preceding one) is dropped from the budget arithmetic. The comment still says "what is left", but it is no longer what is left. Concrete case: the pre-hook run (the `p` argument) took 200 s, `budget` is 600 s, and the always command takes 300 s. The first scope command correctly gets `max(min(600,60), 600-200)=400` s, but the selected-tests command is now given `max(min(600,60), 600-300)=300` s instead of `600-500=100` s. The gate can therefore consume 200+300+300 = 800 s of a 600 s budget before the runner's own timeout fires, i.e. the pass/fail threshold of the gate silently moves further out the more "always" commands are configured. Fix by accumulating elapsed time (e.g. keep a running `spent` seeded with the incoming `p.elapsed_s` and subtracting that).
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/services/ci.py:389 (the `timeout_s=max(...budget - int(p.elapsed_s))` inside the new loop)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:389 (the `timeout_s=max(...budget - int(p.elapsed_s))` inside the new loop)

chunk_findings.detail: When the always command fails (or is unavailable), the loop breaks and `p` is that always-command result, so the *only* check emitted is `selected tests (N + M always): False`. The selected tests never ran, yet the gate evidence asserts a selected-tests failure, and there is no separate `always` entry — which is exactly what the stated intent requires ("recorded in the gate evidence as 'always'"). Input: an `[ci].always_tests` guard such as `tests/test_constants_ratchet.py` failing on an unclassified constant; the operator/merge-pipe reading the gate result sees "selected tests failed" and no indication that the always guard, not the selection, is what broke, so the evidence cannot be used to route the fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:400 (`Check(f"selected tests ({len(scope.tests)} + {len(scope.always)} always)", p.code == 0)`)

chunk_findings.detail: The old code had a deliberate vacuous-pass safeguard: `if not paths: return Plan("full", "no test reaches the change (running none would pass vacuously)")`. The change weakens it to `if not paths and not always`, so the full-suite fallback only fires when *both* the selection and the always set are empty. In practice `always_tests()` returns the default guard files (`tests/test_constants_ratchet.py`, the layering/transcript/readme/tool-budget globs, plus any file containing `ALWAYS = True`), which exist, so `always` is non-empty for essentially every run. Input that demonstrates it: change a standalone `.py` file (not config/unknown, so `_infrastructure` does not force full) that no test imports — the selector yields `paths == []`, `always` is the non-empty guard list, the function now returns `Plan("selected", …)` whose `commands()` is `[always_command]` and runs only the guard files. Previously this exact input ran the whole suite; now a regression in the changed file can pass the gate with only the repo-wide guards having run, which is precisely the "running none would pass vacuously" case the guard exists to prevent. If this reduction is intended it should be stated explicitly, since it removes the safety net for empty-closure changes.

chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci_scope.py — `plan()` (`if not paths and not always` / `always_tests` default set)

chunk_findings.detail: The help text added to the golden snapshot says: "Not in the default, add them when they bite: `tests/test_architecture_guards.py` (18 s), `tests/test_compat*.py`, `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py`". But the default value printed immediately above (and repeated verbatim in `ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.ci.always_tests.toml`) already contains `tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py` and `tests/test_uc_surf_loop_transcript.py`, and both of those files are matched by the pattern `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py`: `test_uc_surf_` + `*`=`setup_ops_`/`loop_` + `transcript` + `*`=empty + `.py`. A user reading `ddflow config` output is therefore told a pattern is excluded from the default when every file it currently matches is in fact run on every selected ci item — the same two transcripts the intent says caused the main failures. The line should either drop the `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py` entry (only `test_architecture_guards.py` and `test_compat*.py` are genuinely outside the default) or reword it to say the pattern's remaining members are not in the default.

chunk_findings.detail: The changed value is the pinned output of a config-dump command, and it now contains `ci.command`, `ci.base`, `ci.timeout_s`, `ci.keep_env`, `ci.on_merge` and the newly added `ci.always_tests` — but it still has **no `ci.tests_scope` entry**, even though that knob is shipped, documented as `default` ("Which tests `ddflow ci run` runs for ONE item (D-test-economy-r2), selected | full. selected (default)…") and is the very knob `ci.always_tests` hangs off ("Test-file globs a selected `ddflow ci run` (see `tests_scope`)…"), and it is referenced by `gates.unit_tests_scope` ("with `[ci].tests_scope = 'selected'` its own selection"). Every other shipped `ci.*` knob appears in this dump with its `source` field; this one does not. So for input "run the transcript against `ddflow config`/`config show` on this tree", either (a) `tests_scope` was never actually registered in the defaults table and the feature is inert, or (b) the pin is stale for it and the transcript test this change is supposed to make green stays red on the `ci` block — the exact class of drift (a knob present in the code/registry but not in the pinned config output) that Bf2d9dab93c was filed about. A regenerated pin must be an exact byte-for-byte snapshot; this one is not self-consistent with the documentation that accompanies it in the same diff.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json (the `ci.*` block of the config dump)

chunk_findings.detail:
The shipped default value for `ci.always_tests` is
`["tests/test_constants_ratchet.py", "tests/test_layering*.py", "tests/golden/**", "tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py", "tests/test_uc_surf_loop_transcript.py", "tests/test_readme_*.py", "tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py"]`,
i.e. it *does* include two files that match `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py`. The same knob's doc string then tells the reader "Not in the default, add them when they bite: … `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py`". The two statements cannot both be true of the shipped default, and the practical consequence is the failure mode this change exists to close: a user (or a future maintainer) who reads that the transcript glob is not in the default will not add it, so a newly added `tests/test_uc_surf_<something>_transcript.py` — a repo-wide guard whose input is the whole code base — silently escapes the always set for every selected-scope `ci run`, exactly as `test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript` and `test_uc_surf_loop_transcript` escaped it before (B116c3f2bc8). Either the default should carry the `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py` glob (as the intent's "the transcript tests" implies), or the "not in the default" list must not name a pattern already covered by it.

chunk_findings.detail: The test picks the *first* directory on `PATH` that ends with the string `"/bin"`, writes a `pytest` shell script there (`write_text`, i.e. it overwrites any existing file), makes it executable and never restores it. `endswith("/bin")` is not a marker of the test fixture's shim directory — it is satisfied by every ordinary bin directory. Given a normal developer/CI `PATH` such as `[REDACTED:path]`, and an activated virtualenv (`.../.venv/bin`) also ending in `/bin`, the first match can easily be a *real* bin directory that already contains `pytest` (or the venv's own pytest) rather than the temp stub dir the fixture creates. The concrete consequences: in a read-only system bin the test dies with `PermissionError` (EACCES) instead of exercising the guard; in a writable one (`[REDACTED:path]`, the venv's `bin`) the real `pytest` executable is silently replaced by a shim that exits 1 on any command whose arguments mention `ratchet` and is left in place after the test, so every later subprocess invocation of `pytest` in the same run — and in the developer's shell afterwards — is poisoned, while the test itself still appears to "pass" because the ratchet command fails either way. The test only works in the exact environment where the fixture's own stub directory is the first `/bin`-suffixed entry, so it is not portable across environments (e.g. when the fixture's dir is named anything other than `.../bin`).

chunk_findings.detail: This change rewrites the tail of the `ci.always_tests` doc so it now explicitly promises the opposite of what the `ci.tests_scope` doc says a few lines above it in the same pinned output. The new `always_tests` text reads "...when the closure is empty they run alone, in place of the whole-suite fallback (the guards are the recall for such a change)", and that is what the code does (`ci_scope.plan()` returns the full-suite plan only `if not paths and not always`, and `always_tests()` is non-empty by default). But the unchanged `ci.tests_scope` block in the same dump still tells the reader: "selected (default) runs ... and runs the whole suite instead when the selector says so (a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, **or no test reaches the change**)". "No test reaches the change" is exactly the empty-closure case that `always_tests` now claims no longer falls back to the whole suite — so a user reading `ddflow config --explain` (the input that produces this pinned transcript) gets two mutually exclusive statements about the same case for the shipped default config, and the `tests_scope` one is the false one after this change. The diff updated the `always_tests` sentence but left the neighbouring `tests_scope` sentence asserting the old behaviour; the golden pin should carry one consistent description (either scope out the case in `tests_scope`, e.g. "no test reaches the change *and no always_tests match*", or drop the fallback claim from `always_tests`).

chunk_findings.detail: The reworded `ci.always_tests` doc in this pin now states: "when the closure is empty they run alone, in place of the whole-suite fallback (the guards are the recall for such a change)". The `ci.tests_scope` entry printed in the *same* `ddflow config --explain` dump (a few entries above, unchanged by this diff) still promises the opposite for exactly that input: "runs the whole suite instead when the selector says so (a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, **or no test reaches the change**)". "No test reaches the change" is precisely the empty closure the new sentence covers, so an operator (or agent) reading the shipped help text gets two mutually exclusive answers for one case: change a file no test imports → `ci.tests_scope` says the whole suite runs, `ci.always_tests` says only the always set runs (which is what the refutation of the vacuous-pass finding says the code now does: `if not paths and not always`). The new doc sentence is right; the sibling `tests_scope` clause it contradicts should have been dropped or qualified in the same change, otherwise the pin documents a behaviour the code no longer has. Either the help text or the code is wrong here, and the pin makes the discrepancy user-visible in every `ddflow config --explain ci.*` / `doctor` output.

chunk_findings.detail: The loop reassigns `p` on every iteration, so `p.elapsed_s` on iteration *i* is only the elapsed time of iteration *i-1* — the elapsed time of the pre-hook result that was passed into the function (and of any command before the immediately preceding one) is dropped from the budget arithmetic. The comment still says "what is left", but it is no longer what is left. Concrete case: the pre-hook run (the `p` argument) took 200 s, `budget` is 600 s, and the always command takes 300 s. The first scope command correctly gets `max(min(600,60), 600-200)=400` s, but the selected-tests command is now given `max(min(600,60), 600-300)=300` s instead of `600-500=100` s. The gate can therefore consume 200+300+300 = 800 s of a 600 s budget before the runner's own timeout fires, i.e. the pass/fail threshold of the gate silently moves further out the more "always" commands are configured. Fix by accumulating elapsed time (e.g. keep a running `spent` seeded with the incoming `p.elapsed_s` and subtracting that).

chunk_findings.detail: When the always command fails (or is unavailable), the loop breaks and `p` is that always-command result, so the *only* check emitted is `selected tests (N + M always): False`. The selected tests never ran, yet the gate evidence asserts a selected-tests failure, and there is no separate `always` entry — which is exactly what the stated intent requires ("recorded in the gate evidence as 'always'"). Input: an `[ci].always_tests` guard such as `tests/test_constants_ratchet.py` failing on an unclassified constant; the operator/merge-pipe reading the gate result sees "selected tests failed" and no indication that the always guard, not the selection, is what broke, so the evidence cannot be used to route the fix.

chunk_findings.detail: The old code had a deliberate vacuous-pass safeguard: `if not paths: return Plan("full", "no test reaches the change (running none would pass vacuously)")`. The change weakens it to `if not paths and not always`, so the full-suite fallback only fires when *both* the selection and the always set are empty. In practice `always_tests()` returns the default guard files (`tests/test_constants_ratchet.py`, the layering/transcript/readme/tool-budget globs, plus any file containing `ALWAYS = True`), which exist, so `always` is non-empty for essentially every run. Input that demonstrates it: change a standalone `.py` file (not config/unknown, so `_infrastructure` does not force full) that no test imports — the selector yields `paths == []`, `always` is the non-empty guard list, the function now returns `Plan("selected", …)` whose `commands()` is `[always_command]` and runs only the guard files. Previously this exact input ran the whole suite; now a regression in the changed file can pass the gate with only the repo-wide guards having run, which is precisely the "running none would pass vacuously" case the guard exists to prevent. If this reduction is intended it should be stated explicitly, since it removes the safety net for empty-closure changes.

chunk_findings.detail:
The shipped default value for `ci.always_tests` is
`["tests/test_constants_ratchet.py", "tests/test_layering*.py", "tests/golden/**", "tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.py", "tests/test_uc_surf_loop_transcript.py", "tests/test_readme_*.py", "tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py"]`,
i.e. it *does* include two files that match `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py`. The same knob's doc string then tells the reader "Not in the default, add them when they bite: … `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py`". The two statements cannot both be true of the shipped default, and the practical consequence is the failure mode this change exists to close: a user (or a future maintainer) who reads that the transcript glob is not in the default will not add it, so a newly added `tests/test_uc_surf_<something>_transcript.py` — a repo-wide guard whose input is the whole code base — silently escapes the always set for every selected-scope `ci run`, exactly as `test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript` and `test_uc_surf_loop_transcript` escaped it before (B116c3f2bc8). Either the default should carry the `tests/test_uc_surf_*transcript*.py` glob (as the intent's "the transcript tests" implies), or the "not in the default" list must not name a pattern already covered by it.

chunk_findings.detail: The test picks the *first* directory on `PATH` that ends with the string `"/bin"`, writes a `pytest` shell script there (`write_text`, i.e. it overwrites any existing file), makes it executable and never restores it. `endswith("/bin")` is not a marker of the test fixture's shim directory — it is satisfied by every ordinary bin directory. Given a normal developer/CI `PATH` such as `[REDACTED:path]`, and an activated virtualenv (`.../.venv/bin`) also ending in `/bin`, the first match can easily be a *real* bin directory that already contains `pytest` (or the venv's own pytest) rather than the temp stub dir the fixture creates. The concrete consequences: in a read-only system bin the test dies with `PermissionError` (EACCES) instead of exercising the guard; in a writable one (`[REDACTED:path]`, the venv's `bin`) the real `pytest` executable is silently replaced by a shim that exits 1 on any command whose arguments mention `ratchet` and is left in place after the test, so every later subprocess invocation of `pytest` in the same run — and in the developer's shell afterwards — is poisoned, while the test itself still appears to "pass" because the ratchet command fails either way. The test only works in the exact environment where the fixture's own stub directory is the first `/bin`-suffixed entry, so it is not portable across environments (e.g. when the fixture's dir is named anything other than `.../bin`).

chunk_findings.detail: This change rewrites the tail of the `ci.always_tests` doc so it now explicitly promises the opposite of what the `ci.tests_scope` doc says a few lines above it in the same pinned output. The new `always_tests` text reads "...when the closure is empty they run alone, in place of the whole-suite fallback (the guards are the recall for such a change)", and that is what the code does (`ci_scope.plan()` returns the full-suite plan only `if not paths and not always`, and `always_tests()` is non-empty by default). But the unchanged `ci.tests_scope` block in the same dump still tells the reader: "selected (default) runs ... and runs the whole suite instead when the selector says so (a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, **or no test reaches the change**)". "No test reaches the change" is exactly the empty-closure case that `always_tests` now claims no longer falls back to the whole suite — so a user reading `ddflow config --explain` (the input that produces this pinned transcript) gets two mutually exclusive statements about the same case for the shipped default config, and the `tests_scope` one is the false one after this change. The diff updated the `always_tests` sentence but left the neighbouring `tests_scope` sentence asserting the old behaviour; the golden pin should carry one consistent description (either scope out the case in `tests_scope`, e.g. "no test reaches the change *and no always_tests match*", or drop the fallback claim from `always_tests`).

chunk_findings.detail: The reworded `ci.always_tests` doc in this pin now states: "when the closure is empty they run alone, in place of the whole-suite fallback (the guards are the recall for such a change)". The `ci.tests_scope` entry printed in the *same* `ddflow config --explain` dump (a few entries above, unchanged by this diff) still promises the opposite for exactly that input: "runs the whole suite instead when the selector says so (a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, **or no test reaches the change**)". "No test reaches the change" is precisely the empty closure the new sentence covers, so an operator (or agent) reading the shipped help text gets two mutually exclusive answers for one case: change a file no test imports → `ci.tests_scope` says the whole suite runs, `ci.always_tests` says only the always set runs (which is what the refutation of the vacuous-pass finding says the code now does: `if not paths and not always`). The new doc sentence is right; the sibling `tests_scope` clause it contradicts should have been dropped or qualified in the same change, otherwise the pin documents a behaviour the code no longer has. Either the help text or the code is wrong here, and the pin makes the discrepancy user-visible in every `ddflow config --explain ci.*` / `doctor` output.

chunk_findings.detail: The change rewrites the whole-suite fallback trigger from "no test reaches the change" to "neither a test nor an `always_tests` file to run". Because the default `always_tests` set is non-empty and its globs (`tests/test_layering*.py`, `tests/golden/**`, the two transcript tests, `tests/test_readme_*.py`, `tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py`, `tests/test_constants_ratchet.py`) always resolve to real files in the repo, the selection can never be empty once the default is in effect. So the fallback for an unreachable change is effectively dead: any change whose file is a normal `.py` file, is not a hub/conftest/pyproject/pre-commit file, and is not in any test's import closure now runs only the fixed guard set instead of the whole suite. For example, a commit that adds `ddflow/tool_main.py` (referenced only from packaging/entry-point metadata or invoked as a subprocess, never imported by a test) previously tripped "no test reaches the change" and ran the whole suite, which executes `tests/test_*_cli_subprocess.py` and catches the failure; with this change the selector reports at least one `always_tests` match, the fallback does not fire, the subprocess test is neither reached nor in `always_tests`, the gate records scope "selected" and passes — exactly the repo-wide failure the change was motivated by (B116c3f2bc8, Bf2d9dab93c). The intent only asks for the always set to run "in addition to the selection"; it does not ask to remove the existing full-suite fallback for changes nothing reaches, and the always globs are a fixed list that by construction cannot cover an arbitrary unreachable source file.

chunk_findings.detail: This change rewrites the tail of the `ci.always_tests` doc so it now explicitly promises the opposite of what the `ci.tests_scope` doc says a few lines above it in the same pinned output. The new `always_tests` text reads "...when the closure is empty they run alone, in place of the whole-suite fallback (the guards are the recall for such a change)", and that is what the code does (`ci_scope.plan()` returns the full-suite plan only `if not paths and not always`, and `always_tests()` is non-empty by default). But the unchanged `ci.tests_scope` block in the same dump still tells the reader: "selected (default) runs ... and runs the whole suite instead when the selector says so (a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, **or no test reaches the change**)". "No test reaches the change" is exactly the empty-closure case that `always_tests` now claims no longer falls back to the whole suite — so a user reading `ddflow config --explain` (the input that produces this pinned transcript) gets two mutually exclusive statements about the same case for the shipped default config, and the `tests_scope` one is the false one after this change. The diff updated the `always_tests` sentence but left the neighbouring `tests_scope` sentence asserting the old behaviour; the golden pin should carry one consistent description (either scope out the case in `tests_scope`, e.g. "no test reaches the change *and no always_tests match*", or drop the fallback claim from `always_tests`).

chunk_findings.detail: The reworded `ci.always_tests` doc in this pin now states: "when the closure is empty they run alone, in place of the whole-suite fallback (the guards are the recall for such a change)". The `ci.tests_scope` entry printed in the *same* `ddflow config --explain` dump (a few entries above, unchanged by this diff) still promises the opposite for exactly that input: "runs the whole suite instead when the selector says so (a hub, conftest, pyproject, the pre-commit config, an unknown file type, **or no test reaches the change**)". "No test reaches the change" is precisely the empty closure the new sentence covers, so an operator (or agent) reading the shipped help text gets two mutually exclusive answers for one case: change a file no test imports → `ci.tests_scope` says the whole suite runs, `ci.always_tests` says only the always set runs (which is what the refutation of the vacuous-pass finding says the code now does: `if not paths and not always`). The new doc sentence is right; the sibling `tests_scope` clause it contradicts should have been dropped or qualified in the same change, otherwise the pin documents a behaviour the code no longer has. Either the help text or the code is wrong here, and the pin makes the discrepancy user-visible in every `ddflow config --explain ci.*` / `doctor` output.

chunk_findings.detail: The change rewrites the whole-suite fallback trigger from "no test reaches the change" to "neither a test nor an `always_tests` file to run". Because the default `always_tests` set is non-empty and its globs (`tests/test_layering*.py`, `tests/golden/**`, the two transcript tests, `tests/test_readme_*.py`, `tests/test_mcp_tool_budget.py`, `tests/test_constants_ratchet.py`) always resolve to real files in the repo, the selection can never be empty once the default is in effect. So the fallback for an unreachable change is effectively dead: any change whose file is a normal `.py` file, is not a hub/conftest/pyproject/pre-commit file, and is not in any test's import closure now runs only the fixed guard set instead of the whole suite. For example, a commit that adds `ddflow/tool_main.py` (referenced only from packaging/entry-point metadata or invoked as a subprocess, never imported by a test) previously tripped "no test reaches the change" and ran the whole suite, which executes `tests/test_*_cli_subprocess.py` and catches the failure; with this change the selector reports at least one `always_tests` match, the fallback does not fire, the subprocess test is neither reached nor in `always_tests`, the gate records scope "selected" and passes — exactly the repo-wide failure the change was motivated by (B116c3f2bc8, Bf2d9dab93c). The intent only asks for the always set to run "in addition to the selection"; it does not ask to remove the existing full-suite fallback for changes nothing reaches, and the always globs are a fixed list that by construction cannot cover an arbitrary unreachable source file.
